question: What are the tech-enablement theses for every company?
html:
Each BSP portfolio company has a named operating system built from proven vendors plus a thin BSP data layer. The aim is to make earnings look more recurring, visible and scalable to the next buyer. For Thomas Scientific the case is EBITDA, not multiple (ServiceOS evidence).

The shared logic

  • Banker data tie exit multiples to repeatable service and retention. PKF shows 5-6x for project-heavy, low-retention firms and 10x+ for repeatable-service firms. Capstone/IMAP expect 6.8x for typical deals versus 9.8x for premium ones (ServiceOS evidence).
  • The evidence supports up to about 3 turns of quality premium. Tech enablement can claim roughly 0.5-2.5 turns of that, depending on the company (ServiceOS evidence).
  • 45 AI agents across six systems put this into practice. Each agent starts on an event and has a named human approver (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Company by company

CompanyOS (vendors)Core thesisPremium turns (est.)Agent value/yr (est.)
Punctual ProsServiceOS (ServiceTitan)Lift booking rates, pricebook use and membership density1.0-2.5$0.88M
CETGridOS (Procore)Turn project work into recurring solar/SCADA and EV O&M0.5-1.5$1.32M
FrontlineFirmOS (ConnectWise/Kaseya)Grow measured security and e-billing revenue-cycle lines0.5-1.5$3.59M
Thomas ScientificLabOS (Shopify Plus/Coupa)Shift to digital transactions; cut cost-to-serve0.5-1.0$3.84M
BPISignalOS (Brandwatch/Zignal)Productize monitoring into repeatable revenue0.5-2.0$2.27M
Fair HarborHarborOS (Shopify/Klaviyo)Cut returns and excess inventoryNot in context$0.77M

Sources: ServiceOS evidence; Portfolio AI-agent plan.

Key support and limits

  • Punctual Pros is the lead case. Call booking averages 38% versus 59% at 25+ technician shops. Pricebook adopters grew tickets 14% versus 8% (ServiceOS evidence). A mid-teens EBITDA margin is the realistic mature target (Public comparables).
  • CET: electrical M&A slowed to 99 deals in 2025, so buyers are more selective. Support strength is medium (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Frontline: entry was already about 12-15x (est.), which limits how much re-rating remains (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Thomas Scientific: Avantor runs about 80% of transactions digitally. Grainger's digital channel grows about 15.6% versus about 2% rep-led. Both points support EBITDA, not a disclosed multiple, and capital structure dominates this exit (ServiceOS evidence).
  • BPI: PPHC trades at about 8.4x versus a 10-13x estimated sponsor exit (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Fair Harbor: the premium range is cut off in the source. The full HarborOS entry in the ServiceOS evidence would answer it.

Caveats

  • The $12.7M program total (est.) rests on analyst volume assumptions. It is not de-duplicated (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
  • The 17-20x roll-up multiples reflect scale and density, not technology alone. Champions (~18.5x) and Sila (~17x) are press estimates (ServiceOS evidence).

Next actions

  • Replace the analyst call, ticket, invoice and member volumes with system-of-record counts at each portfolio company.
  • Pull the complete Fair Harbor and BPI theses from the ServiceOS evidence to fill the gaps above.
  • Set wave 1 baselines (inbound-contact and document agents) before go-live, starting with Punctual Pros booking rate.
  • Test the Frontline premium against its est. 12-15x entry multiple before committing exit-case turns.
